headline: The Senate blocked H.R. 7776, a large defense authorization bill for fiscal year 2023 covering military, intelligence, homeland security, water, and foreign affairs matters, so it did not become law.
what_it_does: If adopted, this measure would have set military end strengths and authorized defense spending and programs for fiscal year 2023. It would also have included military construction projects, Energy Department national security activities, intelligence authorizations, Homeland Security provisions, water resources projects, State Department authorizations, and Coast Guard authorizations. The bill would have addressed many topics, including COVID-19 vaccine requirements for service members, PFAS limits on firefighting gear, aid tied to Ukraine and Taiwan, and new open data rules for financial agencies.

who_it_affects.how: The bill would have set military end strengths, extended certain bonus authorities, and required the Defense Department to rescind its COVID-19 vaccine mandate.
The bill would have expanded Department of Veterans Affairs Vet Center requirements and created a grant pilot to combat food insecurity among veterans and their families.
The bill would have required rare earth magnet contractors to disclose magnet origins and set rules for buying used and remanufactured aircraft parts.
The bill would have presumed certain illnesses to be work-related for federal employees in fire protection activities.
The bill would have barred data brokers from trading certain personal information of federal judges and their families.

who_it_affects.group: Coast Guard personnel and maritime workers
who_it_affects.how: The bill would have authorized new Coast Guard vessels and changed rules on sexual assault reporting and merchant mariner licensing.

who_it_affects.group: Residents near Red Hill Fuel Storage Facility in Hawaii
who_it_affects.how: The bill would have required the Defense Department to defuel the facility and brief Congress on related monitoring efforts.
